explicit_definitions_given: object*: a self-identical physical object existing in a single instant
material object: a sequence of object*s through time
rigid designator: a term that designates the same object in all possible worlds

objections_raised: material objects cannot exist for more than an instant if self-identical
the problem of change and identity over time
the difficulty of identifying object*s in practice

summary_of_core_decisions: The text argues that material objects are not self-identical through time but are sequences of instantaneous object*s. Identity is determined by the object*-sequence history, which is rigidly designated. This allows material objects to be treated as abstract entities, similar to numbers, and resolves the problem of change while preserving rigid designation.
